slot.brief: Two straightforward universal statements and four conclusions; test basic All/Some deduction with Venn logic.

stem:
Read the statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming the statements are true, determine which conclusions follow.

**Statements:**
All lanterns are instruments.
All instruments are portable.

**Conclusions:**
I. All lanterns are portable.
II. Some portable things are instruments.
III. All portable things are lanterns.
IV. No lantern is portable.

verdicts.working: I follows by transitivity: lanterns ⊆ instruments ⊆ portable things. II requires instruments to exist, which the universal statements do not guarantee. III and IV do not follow.
issues: The premises do not assert that any instruments exist, so II is not guaranteed under standard modern logic. Only I follows, but no option lists I alone.

verdicts.working: Lanterns ⊆ Instruments ⊆ Portable. I follows by transitivity. II follows by conversion of 'All instruments are portable' (some portable things are instruments). III reverses the inclusion — invalid. IV contradicts I — invalid.

working:
Lanterns ⊆ instruments ⊆ portable things, so I follows by transitivity. Since instruments exist under the standard syllogism convention, II follows. III reverses the inclusion; IV contradicts the statements. B: III fails; C: IV fails; D: I and II follow.

Independent check: Lanterns ⊆ Instruments ⊆ Portable. I follows by transitivity. II follows by conversion of 'All instruments are portable' (some portable things are instruments). III reverses the inclusion — invalid. IV contradicts I — invalid.
